On 9 July 1986, the Homosexual Law Reform Bill was passed by Parliament after 16 months of debate, marking a landmark moment in our country's history. 🏳️‍🌈🕺\n\r\nTo commemorate this 40-year milestone, we're lighting up the Queens Wharf Sails this Saturday 11 July.\n\r\nThe Homosexual Law Reform Bill was introduced to the House of Representatives by former Wellington City Mayor and MP Fran Wilde. Despite opposition, the campaign succeeded thanks to the determination of advocates and the support of organisations including the New Zealand Homosexual Law Reform Society, the Gay Task Force, Heterosexuals Unafraid of Gays (HUG), the Lesbian Coalition, and the Campaign for Homosexual Equality.\n\r\nWellington has played an important role in this history. The city's first unofficial Pride event, the Newtown Lesbian and Gay Fair, was held in 1986 as part of the campaign for Homosexual Law Reform. The Fair brought people together in support, solidarity and visibility, and quickly became an annual event. \n\r\nThroughout the 90s, the Devotion dance parties transformed the waterfront, beginning as a dusk-to-dawn event at Shed 21 before expanding into a celebration of community and connection. In the 2000s, Out in the Square placed rainbow communities at the heart of the city, followed by Out in the Park at Waitangi Park from 2016. In the 2020s, these events evolved into today's Wellington Pride Festival.\n\r\nAs the queerest city in Aotearoa, we will continue to recognise those who fought for equality, celebrate the progress made over the past 40 years, and acknowledge the work that continues to create a more inclusive Aotearoa New Zealand. 🌈\r\n\n📷 Photo credit: David Hindley","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_forty-years-ago-new-zealand-took-a-significant-activity-7480727816188178433-L75K"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-07-07T22:56:17.458Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_theres-a-new-sculpture-on-wellingtons-waterfront-activity-7480394288921612288-JtXP","text":"There's a new sculpture on Wellington’s waterfront!\n\r\nThis striking installation is the 24th addition to the Wellington Writers Walk honouring Aotearoa New Zealand writers with ties to the capital.\r\n\nInstalled right in time for the Māori New Year, the Walk’s first reo Māori sculpture features the text from He Karakia mō Puanga mā Matariki.\n\r\nThis karakia written by Ben Ngaia (Te Āti Awa) was gifted to Wellingtonians by Te Wharewaka o Pōneke. The sculpture itself was designed by David Hakaraia (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Paoa) and crafted by Human Dynamo Workshop, with landscape design by Tama Whiting (Te Whānau-ā-Apanui).\n\r\nIts placement was chosen strategically for an uninterrupted view of the sea and the sky, towards Matariki as it rises. Find it in the planted area between Te Papa and the waterfront promenade.\n\nThis project is a partnership and collaboration between Wellington Writers Walk and Te Ātiawa/Taranaki Whānui ki Te Upoko o Te Ika, with support from Wellington City Council.\n\nP.S. This sculpture intentionally centres and honours te reo Māori and does not include an English translation. English text is available at https://lnkd.in/eXRffJpZ\n\nImage credit: Kristine Zipfel\r\n","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_theres-a-new-sculpture-on-wellingtons-waterfront-activity-7480394288921612288-JtXP"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-07-03T00:39:40.437Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_weve-officially-reached-500000-visitors-activity-7478608366735630336-iHtz","text":"We’ve officially reached 500,000 visitors at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui!! \n\nAs of lunchtime today, Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui welcomed their 500,000th visitor since reopening in March. \n\nSince then, the library and surrounding Te Ngākau precinct have seen: \n📚 220,000+ books issued \n🤝 2300+ meeting room bookings  \n🔎 150+ archive requests  \n🧵 27,000+ people through the Makerspace \n☕ 800 flat whites each week at Central Ground cafe  \n👕 Increased foot traffic helping local business Honour bring on extra Saturday staff \n🕛 Iris Store + Studio extend its opening hours to seven days a week  \n\nThis celebration is one for the books, with Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui on track to reaching 1.8 million visitors in its first year around – around 4900 people each day.\n\nRead more here: https://lnkd.in/e2WrRr3e","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_weve-officially-reached-500000-visitors-activity-7478608366735630336-iHtz"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-06-26T02:08:12.556Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_wellington-its-time-to-talk-about-amalgamation-activity-7476093932335095808-V0mY","text":"Wellington, it’s time to talk about amalgamation. Should Wellington City merge with other councils in the region? Fill out our survey now.\n\nThe Government has announced it will reform local government by removing regional councils and looking at how other councils can be merged. It has invited councils to form groups and submit proposals for how they could reorganise. If councils don’t make a successful proposal for change, the Government will make the decision on how councils in that region will be structured.\n\nWe’re working with other councils on a proposal, and we want to hear from you.\n\nWhile we welcome social media comments on our posts, please help us ensure your voice is heard by filling out the survey at the link below so we can collate accurate data. Survey feedback will be given to the Mayor and Councillors to inform their decision-making as they consider the proposal.\n\nSurvey closes Sunday 19 July. Follow the link here: wcc.nz/amalgamation","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_wellington-its-time-to-talk-about-amalgamation-activity-7476093932335095808-V0mY"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-06-19T03:17:45.143Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_toi-aro-our-arts-centre-is-coming-to-life-activity-7473574718357278720-lpWv","text":"Toi Aro, our arts centre, is coming to life!  Artists, performers and creative organisations are already making the spaces at 3 Market Lane their own through rehearsals, performances, and exciting new work. 🎉🎊 \n\nToi Aro continues the legacy of Toi Pōneke Arts Centre, which supported artists across film, visual arts, literature, theatre, dance and music for more than 20 years. \n\nThe first event at Toi Aro is Waenga, a play presented by the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa, Te Rākau Hua O Te Wao Tapu Trust, created in partnership with Hurō Productions. \n\nFrom 10 July – 15 October, Te Ara Toi Gallery will host a mana whenua exhibition, featuring powerful artworks, taonga and stories, featuring works from Erenora Puketapu-Hetet, Ariki Brightwell, Hinemoana Baker, Elena Rei, Kauia Moriarty, and more. \n\nContemporary dance is also taking centre stage at Toi Aro, with Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance residents developing and presenting new works through residencies supported by Footnote NZ Dance, Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance and the Hannah Playhouse. 🩰 💃 \n\nToi Aro is also proud to welcome resident artists and organisations including SOUNZ, Kavanah Productions, Arts Access Aotearoa, Workspace Studios, NZ Comedy School and Dead Teapot Ltd, along with independent artists. \n\nThe vibrant June – July programme is underway, and it is only just the beginning! 🤝 \n\n📷 Image credit to: Māori theatre company Te Rākau Hua o Te Wao Tapu prepare for their play Waenga at Toi Aro arts centre.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_toi-aro-our-arts-centre-is-coming-to-life-activity-7473574718357278720-lpWv"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-06-03T04:40:28.736Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_the-p%C5%8Dneke-waterfront-is-set-to-welcome-a-activity-7467797331329957888-fNMq","text":"The Pōneke waterfront is set to welcome a new addition to the Writers Walk: the first new sculpture since 2013, and the first written entirely in te reo Māori.\n\nSince its launch in 2002, the Walk has grown to 23 sculptural quotations honouring Aotearoa New Zealand writers with ties to Wellington. It celebrates and commemorates the place of Wellington in these writers’ lives, and their place in the life of Wellington, promoting local literature to a wider public, including visitors to the capital.\n\nThe upcoming sculpture features He Karakia mō Puanga mā Matariki, composed by Ben Ngaia (Te Āti Awa). Designer Dave Hakaraia (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Paoa) is creating the sculpture, with landscape design by Tama Whiting (Te Whānau‑ā‑Apanui) and production by Human Dynamo Workshop.\n\nChosen in association with Mana Whenua and Wellington City Council, the location will provide the readers an uninterrupted view of the sea and sky.\n\nIt's expected to be in place by the end of June, just in time for Matariki.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_the-p%C5%8Dneke-waterfront-is-set-to-welcome-a-activity-7467797331329957888-fNMq"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil"},"datePublished":"2026-05-21T23:00:27.789Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_toip%C5%8Dneke-arts-centre-has-been-re-imagined-activity-7463363109160931328-OMRS","text":"Toi Pōneke  Arts Centre has been re-imagined with a new name, location, vision, and kaupapa, to better support the city’s creative sector. 🎭🧑‍🎨\r\n\r\nThe new arts centre is opening in late June at 3 Market Lane in central Wellington, under the name ‘Toi Aro’, gifted by mana whenua. It builds on the legacy of Toi Pōneke Arts Centre which, for more than 20 years, supported artists across film, visual arts, literature, theatre, dance and music. Toi Pōneke artists have gone on to present work locally, nationally and internationally, contributing to Wellington’s role as a centre for creative practice.  \r\n\r\nDesigned to be inclusive and physically accessible to all, Toi Aro is grounded in mana whenua kawa and tikanga, and will operate as a Tiriti-led facility. The centre provides rental artist studios and arts offices, exhibition opportunities, brand new hireable spaces for creative sector use, artist residencies, public programmes, and a range of activities and events. \r\n\r\nLearn more about Toi Aro through the link below 👇","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/wellingtoncitycouncil_toip%C5%8Dneke-arts-centre-has-been-re-imagined-activity-7463363109160931328-OMRS"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Wellington City Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/wellingtoncitycouncil","address":{"type":"PostalAddress","streetAddress":"113 The Terrace","addressLocality":"Wellington City","addressRegion":"Wellington","postalCode":"6011","addressCountry":"NZ"},"description":"Wellington is a vibrant city with a thriving cultural life, talented people, and cutting-edge businesses.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Forty years ago, New Zealand took a significant step forward for LGBTQIA+ rights. On 9 July 1986, the Homosexual Law Reform Bill was passed by Parliament after 16 months of debate, marking a landmark moment in our country's history. 🏳️🌈🕺

To commemorate this 40-year milestone, we're lighting up the Queens Wharf Sails this Saturday 11 July.

The Homosexual Law Reform Bill was introduced to the House of Representatives by former Wellington City Mayor and MP Fran Wilde. Despite opposition, the campaign succeeded thanks to the determination of advocates and the support of organisations including the New Zealand Homosexual Law Reform Society, the Gay Task Force, Heterosexuals Unafraid of Gays (HUG), the Lesbian Coalition, and the Campaign for Homosexual Equality.

Wellington has played an important role in this history. The city's first unofficial Pride event, the Newtown Lesbian and Gay Fair, was held in 1986 as part of the campaign for Homosexual Law Reform. The Fair brought people together in support, solidarity and visibility, and quickly became an annual event. 

Throughout the 90s, the Devotion dance parties transformed the waterfront, beginning as a dusk-to-dawn event at Shed 21 before expanding into a celebration of community and connection. In the 2000s, Out in the Square placed rainbow communities at the heart of the city, followed by Out in the Park at Waitangi Park from 2016. In the 2020s, these events evolved into today's Wellington Pride Festival.

As the queerest city in Aotearoa, we will continue to recognise those who fought for equality, celebrate the progress made over the past 40 years, and acknowledge the work that continues to create a more inclusive Aotearoa New Zealand. 🌈

📷 Photo credit: David Hindley</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">There's a new sculpture on Wellington’s waterfront!

This striking installation is the 24th addition to the Wellington Writers Walk honouring Aotearoa New Zealand writers with ties to the capital.

Installed right in time for the Māori New Year, the Walk’s first reo Māori sculpture features the text from He Karakia mō Puanga mā Matariki.

This karakia written by Ben Ngaia (Te Āti Awa) was gifted to Wellingtonians by Te Wharewaka o Pōneke. The sculpture itself was designed by David Hakaraia (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Paoa) and crafted by <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/human-dynamo-workshop?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Human Dynamo Workshop</a>, with landscape design by Tama Whiting (Te Whānau-ā-Apanui).

Its placement was chosen strategically for an uninterrupted view of the sea and the sky, towards Matariki as it rises. Find it in the planted area between Te Papa and the waterfront promenade.

This project is a partnership and collaboration between Wellington Writers Walk and Te Ātiawa/Taranaki Whānui ki Te Upoko o Te Ika, with support from Wellington City Council.

P.S. This sculpture intentionally centres and honours te reo Māori and does not include an English translation. English text is available at <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/eXRffJpZ?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/eXRffJpZ</a>

Image credit: Kristine Zipfel
</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Toi Aro, our arts centre, is coming to life!  Artists, performers and creative organisations are already making the spaces at 3 Market Lane their own through rehearsals, performances, and exciting new work. 🎉🎊 

Toi Aro continues the legacy of Toi Pōneke Arts Centre, which supported artists across film, visual arts, literature, theatre, dance and music for more than 20 years. 

The first event at Toi Aro is Waenga, a play presented by the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa, Te Rākau Hua O Te Wao Tapu Trust, created in partnership with Hurō Productions. 

From 10 July – 15 October, Te Ara Toi Gallery will host a mana whenua exhibition, featuring powerful artworks, taonga and stories, featuring works from Erenora Puketapu-Hetet, Ariki Brightwell, Hinemoana Baker, Elena Rei, Kauia Moriarty, and more. 

Contemporary dance is also taking centre stage at Toi Aro, with Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance residents developing and presenting new works through residencies supported by Footnote NZ Dance, Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance and the Hannah Playhouse. 🩰 💃 

Toi Aro is also proud to welcome resident artists and organisations including SOUNZ, Kavanah Productions, Arts Access Aotearoa, Workspace Studios, NZ Comedy School and Dead Teapot Ltd, along with independent artists. 

The vibrant June – July programme is underway, and it is only just the beginning! 🤝 

📷 Image credit to: Māori theatre company Te Rākau Hua o Te Wao Tapu prepare for their play Waenga at Toi Aro arts centre.</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The Pōneke waterfront is set to welcome a new addition to the Writers Walk: the first new sculpture since 2013, and the first written entirely in te reo Māori.

Since its launch in 2002, the Walk has grown to 23 sculptural quotations honouring Aotearoa New Zealand writers with ties to Wellington. It celebrates and commemorates the place of Wellington in these writers’ lives, and their place in the life of Wellington, promoting local literature to a wider public, including visitors to the capital.

The upcoming sculpture features He Karakia mō Puanga mā Matariki, composed by Ben Ngaia (Te Āti Awa). Designer Dave Hakaraia (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Paoa) is creating the sculpture, with landscape design by Tama Whiting (Te Whānau‑ā‑Apanui) and production by <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/human-dynamo-workshop?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Human Dynamo Workshop</a>.

Chosen in association with Mana Whenua and Wellington City Council, the location will provide the readers an uninterrupted view of the sea and sky.

It's expected to be in place by the end of June, just in time for Matariki.</p>
